East Breifne.fact: Tomas Mór provided refuge and support to rivals of King Tiernan Mór O'Rourke of West Breifne in the late 1370s and 1380s, prompting O'Rourke to invade East Breifne in 1390.

East Breifne.fact: This was in competition to Eoghan na Feosaige, Seoan's son, who was supported by the English government in Dublin and the Anglo-Normans in Meath. This ploy to get the English to support his claim alienated him from his kinsmen.

East Breifne.fact: The O’Reilly sept and their allies continued to exclude Eoghan na Fesoagie from the kingship and elected Risdeard, son of King Tomas (1384-1392), as king following Mealmordha's death in 1411.

East Breifne.fact: The O’Reilly sept and their allies continued to exclude Eoghan na Fesoagie from the kingship and elected Risdeard, son of King Tomas (1384-1392), as king following Mealmordha's death in 1411. East Breifne.subject: Indian Society

East Breifne.fact: With few suitable heirs available the O'Reilly nobles recalled Eoghan na Feosaige, who finally assumed the kingship in 1418.

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society

East Breifne.fact: Eoghan stationed soldiers in Carrigallen to defend and support Art in 1419.

East Breifne.fact: The war's origins can be traced back to a disagreement between Sean and Fearghal O’Reilly. Sean and his allies supported Eoghan na Feosaige as king, while Fearghal and his supporters argued that Fearghal was the rightful ruler of East Breifne.

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society

East Breifne.fact: He eventually killed his brother Sean to solidify his position as the chief of Clan Mahon before launching a full-scale rebellion against Eoghan na Feosaige in 1427.

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society

East Breifne.fact: Fearghal had assembled a seemingly insurmountable force that included the MacCabes, a military clan from within East Breifne, King Tadhg O’Rourke of West Breifne, who had emerged victorious from the war of succession, as well as Richard Talbot the Lord Chancellor of Ireland. East Breifne.fact: In what would become a watershed moment in East Breifne's history that would see it firmly align itself with Ulster and drift away from the sphere of Connacht, Eoghan na Feosaige departed the kingdom that year and turned out of desperation to Eoghan O’Neill, King of Tyrone, for help. East Breifne.fact: The forces of O’Neill and his allies marched south and met with those of Fearghal, Talbot, O’Rourke and MacCabe at Achadh-cille-moire. East Breifne.subject: Indian Society

East Breifne.fact: With the long disaffected claimant Fearghal still living, another dispute over the kingship was inevitable. East Breifne.fact: The virulently anti-English O’Neill took aim at every lord who co-operated with them and by 1560 was the undisputed ruler of Ulster "from Drogheda to Erne".

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society
East Breifne.question: In 1538 with his position secure, O’Reilly joined the _____ and gave strong support to their expeditions into Ulster against the Geraldine League
East Breifne.fact: Lord Deputy Leonard Grey demanded that O’Reilly join the English against the rebel league, but he refused due to internal instability and the insecurity of his position. East Breifne.subject: Indian Society
East Breifne.question: Maolmordha died in 1565 and was succeeded by _____
East Breifne.fact: Maolmordha died in 1565 and was succeeded by Aodh Connallach.

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society
East Breifne.question: Aodh gave up his son John to _____ in 1575
East Breifne.fact: Upon coming to power he rebelled against Tyrone and supported Sidney against Shane O’Neill and his successor Turlough Luineach in the early 1570s. In turn, Sidney helped Aodh crush dissent against his kingship domestically.

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society
East Breifne.question: The Annals of the _____ record that Pilib crushed an attempted invasion by the O'Neills in 1581, before negotiating a peace with them later that year
East Breifne.fact: The Annals of the Four Masters record that Pilib crushed an attempted invasion by the O'Neills in 1581, before negotiating a peace with them later that year.

East Breifne.fact: This prompted the Norman invasion of Ireland in 1169. With Norman aid Mac Murchada retook Leinster, and set Kells, Breifne's easternmost outpost, ablaze.

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society
East Breifne.question: In 1170 Breifne was invaded and in the following years the kingdom was carved up by the _____
East Breifne.fact: In 1170 Breifne was invaded and in the following years the kingdom was carved up by the Normans. However, the O'Reilly allied themselves with the Normans as a way of breaking free of the O'Rourke.

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society

East Breifne.fact: With Norman aid Mac Murchada retook Leinster, and set Kells, Breifne's easternmost outpost, ablaze. O'Rourke power was weakened whilst the O'Reilly submitted to Mac Murchada and his Norman allies during the conquest.

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society
East Breifne.question: The influence of the _____ in eastern Breifne was considerable and by 1211 they had established castles in Belturbet and Kilmore

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society

East Breifne.fact: By 1220 de Lacy had taken control of most of the O'Reilly territory, including the stony island at Lough Oughter, where William Gorm began construction of a castle. East Breifne.subject: Indian Society

East Breifne.fact: By the Autumn of 1242, when it had become apparent that Tadhg had garnered little support for his claim and was no longer of any use to Cúchonnacht, he was seized and imprisoned.

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society

East Breifne.fact: Cu Chonnacht retired in 1365 and passed the title to his brother Pilib. Upon his accession, Pilib confronted the Bishop of Kilmore Riocard O'Reilly, his brother Maelseachleann's son.

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society
East Breifne.question: Seoan O'_____ was made king in 1392

On his way to Drumlane to submit to Tomas Mór, the Clan Muircheartaigh attempted to assassinate Tiernan Mór, possibly in an unsuccessful attempt to curry favour with the O’Reillys and return from exile.

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society

East Breifne.fact: Eoghan na Feosaige had defeated the rebellion against him and defended his title, but at a cost. Following Eoghan na Feosaige's allegiance to O’Neill, the O’Reillys appear multiple times in the annals partaking in Tyrone's various wars across Ulster, illustrating East Breifne's position as a vassal state of Tyrone.

East Breifne.fact: This was in competition to Eoghan na Feosaige, Seoan's son, who was supported by the English government in Dublin and the Anglo-Normans in Meath.

East Breifne.fact: He also received the support of Eoghan na Feosaige's brother Domnall and James Butler, 4th Earl of Ormond. What could’ve spiraled into a protracted war of succession was avoided when Domnall dropped his support for Fearghal and backed his nephew Sean an Einigh in 1450.

By 1580 Aodh's health had declined dramatically and he retreated from public life, although still officially the king.

East Breifne.fact: The decision left both Pilib and Emon disaffected and they continued to challenge John's rule.

East Breifne.subject: Indian Society

East Breifne.fact: John's legal expertise allowed him to put forward a strong defence of his right to the kingship and it was decided by the council that he should receive the title. The decision left both Pilib and Emon disaffected and they continued to challenge John's rule.

East Breifne.fact: O’Reilly and Perrot toured East Breifne and met with the ruling clans for over a year until late 1584.

East Breifne.fact: The controversial agreement was designed to hasten the transformation of Cavan into a fully-fledged English-style county.

Vietnamese Cambodians also lived further upstream along the shores of the Tonlé Sap.
